## Series Overview

Every post in the [Synthetic Data Series](../synthetic-data/index.qmd) generates a single static
image. Real industrial inspection is often a video problem -- radioscopy scan heads and conveyors
moving parts past an X-ray detector, with real ambient mechanical sound alongside the picture.
This series asks whether general-purpose joint video+audio generation models, applied to that real
domain, actually stay *in* that domain -- or quietly drift back to whatever they were trained on
most.

Same ethos as the rest of this blog: real code, real captured output, honest limitations reported
alongside anything that works.

### Posts in this series

1. **Part 1** -- [X-ray Inspection Video + Sound Generation](01-xray-inspection-video-sound.qmd).
   A real GDXray weld radiograph, LTX-2 (a real, non-gated 19B joint video+audio diffusion
   transformer, int4-quantized to fit real memory constraints), and a real, honest failure mode:
   the model holds the X-ray domain faithfully for the one real conditioning frame, then drifts
   into ordinary color industrial photography for the rest of the generated motion.
